Subject: AcmeHealth - GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Jamie —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the GDPR/compliance items we discussed: 

1) SOC 2 / security posture
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; I can share the most recent report and a secure download link for your security team (see link below).

2) GDPR roles (controller vs processor)
- From our conversation it sounded like AcmeHealth will act as the Controller and Redwood Inference as the Processor. Please confirm if that is correct for your legal/compliance team.

3) DPA & SCCs
- Attached is a Redwood DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Draft.docx) and an SCC selection matrix (SCC_selection_matrix.csv) to make module selection easier. For most SaaS inference customers we recommend Module 2 with the EU SCCs for controller->processor relationships, but we can align to your legal preference.

4) Vendor security questionnaire
- I’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire template and would appreciate it if you could send back Acme’s completed questionnaire or confirm which fields you’d like us to pre-fill.

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm controller/processor roles (one-line reply).
- If you’re aligned, can you: (a) review the attached DPA draft and highlight any major redlines and (b) indicate preferred SCC module (we recommended Module 2).
- I’ll loop in legal to execute the DPA once terms are agreed; Rishi and Neha from our privacy/security teams are cc’d for quick turnaround on the SCC selection and SOC 2 evidence.

Links/attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft.docx, SCC_selection_matrix.csv, Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf; SOC 2 report: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/soc2/Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call with your legal/security folks if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Rishi / Neha — forwarding thread with AcmeHealth (see below). They confirmed Controller = Acme, prefer Module 2. They want slightly tighter sub-processor notice and clarity on data retention windows. Timeline: they hope to have initial read in ~5 business days pending SOC2 + tightened DPA.

Actions I need from you (quick):
- Rishi: can you confirm we’re comfortable with Module 2 for this customer and whether any additional contractual language is advisable around international sub-processors? Please flag any non-starters.
- Neha: please review the attached DPA draft and propose redlines specifically for: (a) sub-processor notice and prior consent vs. post-notification, (b) retention periods for request/response logs (they care about granularity), and (c) audit access scope.

Notes/constraints to consider:
- We generally avoid prior consent for each sub-processor but can provide 30-day notice plus an approved sub-processor list; if Acme insists on prior consent we should quantify escalation risk to the deal (slower execution).
- For retention, Redwood retains inference logs for 90 days by default and can offer 12/24 month retention add-ons for enterprise plans — indicate this as an option.

I’ll prepare an initial redline to the DPA for your review (target EOD Monday) and propose legal@redwoodinference.com as primary contact to iterate. Let me know if you want me to set a 30-min sync with Acme legal early next week.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive
